symptom: `alter page … set (ColumnWidth: manual, Size: 220) on dg column(Name)` then `set (ColumnWidth: autoFill) …` stored width=autoFill with size=220 and mx check reported CE0463 on the Data grid 2 (11.6.6 and 11.15.0, 1 error; the reporter's workaround was `autoFill` with `Size: 1`) (mendixlabs/mxcli#1519 item 3b)
cause: `setColumnPropertyMut` (mdl/backend/pagemutator/mutator.go) writes exactly the property named and leaves the properties the widget hides BECAUSE of it at whatever they held. Data grid 2 3.x hides `size` unless width is "manual", `minWidth` unless width is "autoFit", `minWidthLimit` unless minWidth is "manual"; a hidden property holding a non-default value is CE0463. The create path writes them at their default; ALTER never re-evaluated
file: `mdl/backend/pagemutator/column_hidden_reset.go` (`ResetHiddenColumnProperties`, `resetHiddenItemProps` — defaults from the STORED Type, iterated to a fixpoint for cascades), `mdl/backend/mutation.go` (optional `backend.ColumnHiddenPropertyResetter`), `mdl/executor/cmd_alter_page.go` (`applySetPropertyMutator` → `resetHiddenColumnProperties` with rules lifted from the installed .mpk), `mdl/executor/validate_alter_set.go` (check judges a column SET whole as well as per property)
insight: **A setter that changes one property must re-ask which OTHER properties are now hidden** — the dependency is the widget's (editorConfig `hidePropertyIn(…,"columns",o,"size")`, lifted as a nested item-scope rule), so take the rules from the installed package and the defaults from the stored Type rather than special-casing `size`. A hidden property the same statement names is refused rather than silently reset (`ColumnWidth: autoFill, Size: 220`); its default (`Size: 1`) is accepted. Check's per-property dry run had to stop applying the follow-up: judged alone, `Size: 220` of `ColumnWidth: manual, Size: 220` is hidden under the stored autoFill and was refused — the first measurement run caught that, the unit tests did not. Test the whole-statement probe as well as the per-property one.
